title: Veridian Networks POC kickoff - security, SLA & benchmark plan
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC. Primary asks from Veridian: SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and audit trails, throughput target ~200 qps with 99th pct latency target and roll-out plan. Redwood to provide security pack, propose benchmark test window, and share pricing for dedicated vs hosted pilot.
action_items: Jared Bennett - Send SOC 2 + ISO summary pack and compliance matrix - due 2025-09-11
Maya Liu - Draft benchmark plan with sample prompts/seq lengths and expected metrics (p95/p99/tokens) - due 2025-09-12
Veridian (Raj) - Share representative request logs/sample dataset (anonymized) and SLO targets - due 2025-09-15
Claire O'Neill - Confirm required retention period for audit logs and KMS integration details - due 2025-09-14
Priya Menon - Schedule hands-on benchmark window and follow-up technical deep dive - due 2025-09-16
next_steps: Redwood to email security artifacts and compliance FAQ
Agree benchmark window and provide dataset by 2025-09-15
Kick off test bench on Redwood Dedicated capacity (draft pricing) week of 2025-09-22
Schedule SE deep dive on SSO/SAML + SCIM integration
transcript:
Header: 2025-09-09 14:30 PDT | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes | Attendees: Jared, Maya, Rohit, Priya (Redwood); Anna, Raj, Claire, Tom, Luis (Veridian)

[00:00] Jared Bennett: Hi everyone thanks for joining, Jared here from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Anna Khatri: Anna Khatri here, Head of AI at Veridian.
[00:11] Raj Patel: Raj, infra.
[00:12] Claire O'Neill: Claire, information security.
[00:14] Tom Reyes: Tom, product.
[00:15] Luis Mendez: Luis, SRE.
[00:17] Maya Liu: Maya from Redwood, I'll be running the benchmarks and helping with the integration.
[00:20] Rohit Desai: Rohit -- solutions engineering, happy to jump into the deeper perf stuff.

[00:25] Jared Bennett: Cool. Goal of today's call is to scope the POC — success criteria, security/compliance gating, workload sizing and a benchmark plan. We think a six week window is reasonable, but we'll confirm. Any immediate constraints from your side?
[00:40] Anna Khatri: Major constraint is regulatory — we need SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 evidence before legal green light. Also SSO with SAML and SCIM to provision roles. Data residency does not have to be on-prem for pilot, but we do need audit logs and KMS for keys.
[01:01] Claire O'Neill: To add, we're strict about retention windows for logs and proof of deletion. We also require RBAC that maps to our internal roles. We may need an on-prem option if the pilot shows PHI will surface, but for now cloud VPC is okay.
[01:18] Raj Patel: On infra sizing — we expect 150–200 qps during peak for inference in the pilot, roughly 8 to 12 tokens per request on average but we have spikes up to 120 tokens for longer sequences. Latency targets are p95 under 120ms for the short calls, and p99 < 250ms ideally. Cost is a factor; we'd like to compare hosted vs dedicated capacity.

[01:45] Maya Liu: Thanks Raj, that's helpful. A couple clarifications: when you say 150–200 qps is that concurrent requests or sustained per second? Also are those across many short prompts or batched?
[02:00] Raj Patel: Sustained per second. Most are short prompts at about 8 tokens, but long tail exists for a small percentage. We rarely batch client-side; want server-side batching if possible.

[02:10] Rohit Desai: Server-side continuous batching and prefix/KV cache can help a lot — we usually enable prefix caching for repetitive session traffic. Note the transcript may say KV cash occasionally, our auto-transcript messes that up.

[02:25] Tom Reyes: On success criteria from product POV: 1) latency under p95 threshold, 2) functional parity on our golden prompts (we'll provide 50 reference prompts), 3) clear audit logs with user attribution, and 4) a plan for roll to staging after pilot.

[02:45] Claire O'Neill: For compliance — we want SOC 2 evidence (AICPA report), ISO 27001 cert, SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with admin/auditor/developer roles, and immutable audit logs for 90 days at minimum. KMS integration for customer-managed keys is preferred.

[03:10] Maya Liu: Understood. We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary, and we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. For KMS we support both cloud KMS and HSM integrations depending on your private deployment. For the pilot we typically propose a VPC Private deployment with our control plane or a private control plane if you want.

[03:32] Anna Khatri: What do you mean by private control plane? That raises red flags for us unless it's customer-managed.
[03:36] Priya Menon: Priya chiming in — private control plane means the control plane is in your VPC with RBAC and audit logs flowing to your logging endpoint; it's a paid enterprise option. We'll include the architecture diagram in the security pack.

[03:52] Raj Patel: For benchmarks, we need p95 and p99 latency, tokens per second cost, and memory/kv cache behaviour for longer sequences. Can you run both hosted and dedicated tests so we can see delta?
[04:05] Maya Liu: Yes, we can run a head-to-head. Typical plan: one week of cold-start tests, then a sustained load test for 48 hours to capture steady-state, and a few spike tests. We'll need a representative dataset and the 50 golden prompts Tom mentioned.

[04:20] Luis Mendez: On observability — we need per-request traces, token-level cost breakdown, and per-model dashboards. Does Redwood provide distributed tracing headers?
[04:30] Rohit Desai: We support tracing hooks and per-request metadata; we can surface token-level cost breakdown in the console and stream logs to your SIEM. There's a small footnote that some proprietary telemetry names get sanitized — just a transcription quirk.

[04:45] Claire O'Neill: Encryption — are payloads encrypted at rest and in transit? And what about metadata in logs?
[04:52] Maya Liu: All traffic is TLS1.2+ in transit. At rest we encrypt and can support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For logs, we can either redact PII at ingestion or stream raw logs into your own logging bucket — depends on your preference. We'll document options.

[05:10] Anna Khatri: Tying success criteria to sign-off: our legal/security wants SOC 2 evidence and SSO integration completed, product wants golden prompt accuracy >95% exact match for classification tasks (we can be flexible on generation tasks with BLEU/ROUGE thresholds), SRE wants p95 < 120ms and p99 < 250ms for 90% of steady-state windows. If these are met and costs are within 15% of projection, we'll consider moving to a staged rollout.

[05:40] Jared Bennett: Great — summarizing: Redwood to provide security pack and sign posting on KMS/Private control plane options, SE team to run a proposed benchmark plan, Veridian to provide sample dataset and golden prompts, and we'll schedule the 48-hour sustained test. Any other constraints?

[05:55] Tom Reyes: Timeline: we want the bench to run by 9/22 if possible — product roadmap is tight.
[05:59] Priya Menon: We can target the week of 9/22 for the bench window. We'll provision Dedicated capacity for that window and provide pricing options for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot.

[06:10] Claire O'Neill: One question on RBAC — can Redwood map to our internal groups via SCIM and support an "auditor" role that has readonly access to logs but no model config?
[06:20] Rohit Desai: Yes, SCIM mapping and role-mapping is supported. Auditor role is common; we can ensure segregation and provide immutable export of logs to an external bucket for compliance.

[06:35] Raj Patel: Also can you test sequence caching behavior? For our workload prefix caching matters for sessions. We need to understand cache hit rate and fallback behavior if cache is warmed/unwarmed.
[06:45] Maya Liu: We'll include cache warmup tests and report KV cache hit rates. Note the transcript autocaption sometimes writes KV cash — ignore that.

[06:55] Anna Khatri: Regarding pricing — if dedicated is significantly cheaper per unit and meets latency, we'll prefer dedicated. But if hosted gives faster ops and security pack is equivalent, we may go hosted to start. So we need a clear cost per 1M tokens and an estimated monthly run rate.

[07:20] Jared Bennett: We'll include a cost model in the follow-up. We'll also surface tradeoffs between autoscaling in Dedicated vs bursting on Hosted.

[07:35] Luis Mendez: For SSO — we use Okta. We need SAML 2.0 IdP initiated login and SCIM provisioning. Can you do test integration with our dev Okta tenant?
[07:45] Priya Menon: Yes, we'll coordinate with Claire and Raj to do an Okta test. We'll send a setup doc and sample metadata file.

[07:55] Claire O'Neill: Audit trail requirements: immutable logs with at least user/principal ID, request payload hash, model version, latency, and whether KMS was used. Retention 90 days then archived for 1 year. Also need exportable evidence in a format our auditors accept (CSV + JSON).

[08:22] Maya Liu: We can provide all those fields. For request payload hashes we can compute a SHA256 on ingress and log that. We'll include example log snippets in the security pack.

[08:40] Tom Reyes: One more product ask — model pinning and rollback policy in case of quality regressions. Can Redwood pin a model version for the pilot and have automatic fallback to a baseline?
[08:50] Rohit Desai: Yes, we support model version pinning, canary rollout, and automatic rollback based on error rates or quality regressions from eval hooks. We'll demo that in the follow-up SE deep dive.

[09:05] Anna Khatri: Ok are we comfortable with the 6-week pilot? Week 1: security review + provisioning; Week 2: dataset ingest + smoke tests; Week 3–4: benchmarks (including the 48 hour run); Week 5: analysis + tuning; Week 6: decision and handoff.

[09:25] Jared Bennett: That timeline aligns with our usual POC cadence. We'll send a draft project plan.

[09:32] Claire O'Neill: If any failed controls show up, we'll need mitigation plans before sign-off — e.g., if audit logs show sensitive fields, we need an agreed redaction flow.

[09:42] Priya Menon: We'll include mitigation patterns in the security pack and a runbook for dealing with common findings.

[09:50] Luis Mendez: Curious — do we get raw access to kernels/metrics when Dedicated is provisioned? We want to see GPU metrics and memory pressure.
[09:58] Rohit Desai: We expose an agent and dashboards and can stream metrics to your Prometheus or Grafana; full kernel-level is limited for hosted environments but Dedicated gives more telemetry. We'll include sample dashboards.

[10:18] Anna Khatri: Sounds good. I'm comfortable.

[10:22] Jared Bennett: Final recap of action items: we'll circulate the security pack and SOC2 docs, Maya will share the benchmark plan, Raj will share sample dataset, Claire will confirm retention/KMS, and Priya will set the benchmark window for week of 9/22. Any objections?
[10:38] Claire O'Neill: No objections.
[10:40] Raj Patel: No.
[10:42] Tom Reyes: Go ahead.
[10:43] Jared Bennett: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and log actions in the shared doc.
[10:48] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-attributions and small ASR errors (KV cash, etc.). References shared: Security pack link (to be sent), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), Okta test metadata.
